name: BSP_GameTuning_LoadFromPlaneGlobals
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall constructor of the 6D0h-byte plane tuning singleton; ECX = the operator new(0x6d0) block from 0042E7A2, returns this, body 007E2A20-007EAB5E. Stores vtable 00d08628 at 007E2A4C, runs Scripts\global\luaMW_init.lua at 007E2AE9 (constants and the DEG/KMH helpers only, no key read from it) and Scripts\datatables\PlaneGlobals.lua at 007E2B5D, then fetches the global PlaneGlobals table at 007E2BB4 and copies 423 distinct key paths into 436 offsets with 439 stores. No constructor defaults: the block is not zeroed. See docs/GAME_TUNING_SINGLETON.md. | Mirror step recovered (packet cc7_rate_clamp). After reading the Lua tables into this+210h..348h it publishes the whole 312-byte block to globals in one instruction: 007EAAD7 MOV ECX,4Eh (78 dwords), 007EAADC MOV EDI,0F872F0h, 007EAAE1 REP MOVSD with bytes F3 A5 - a copy from ESI, not a STOSD fill. ESI is EBP+210h from 007E2D03 and is provably unchanged across the 6250 instructions in between: the function mentions it fifteen times and writes it exactly twice (XOR ESI,ESI at 007E2A61 and that LEA). EBP is the this pointer (007E2A42 MOV EBP,ECX). Consequence: the copy carries an xref only on 00F872F0, so the other 77 globals it writes - including the rotation factors at 00F872FC/300/304 that 007DA710 reads - appear unwritten to Ghidra's xref table while sitting in the uninitialised part of .data, which makes their static 0.0 loader zero-fill rather than data. docs/PLANE_CONTROL_RATE_LAW.md.

name: BSP_PlaneSquadron_AssignFormationIndices
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc8_formation, read from the listing, complete. __thiscall(squadron), RET at 007ED374, body 007ED260-007ED374, 83 instructions. Two walks over the +3CCh live members of +3D0h with a five-entry table on the stack whose values are 0 (never seen), 1 (a member carries that index now) and -1 (handed out this pass). 007ED2C7 PUSH EDI shifts the frame four bytes between the walks, which is why the first writes [ESP+ESI*4+0Ch] and the second reads [ESP+EAX*4+10h]: the same slot. First walk 007ED290-007ED2B4: member+9D8h = i at 007ED292, then taken[member+9D0h] = 1 at 007ED2AC. Second walk 007ED2C8-007ED367: slot 0 takes index 0 at 007ED2D2 and marks taken[0] = -1; every other slot takes the lowest free ODD index from 1 (007ED2E1 CMP [ESP+14h],0 with the JGE at 007ED2FB, then 007ED300-007ED308) and the lowest free EVEN index from 2 (007ED30A-007ED319) and keeps the smaller (007ED33E-007ED35A). 007ED31B-007ED33A pushes a member that already carries a positive EVEN index to the next odd one when the two candidates are adjacent, which keeps a plane on its side across a re-assignment. A fresh three-plane squadron, all members at 0, gets 0, 1, 2. Callers 007ED610 PromoteFlightLeader, 007F3970 RemovePlane and 009BED80, the latter reached from 009C7240 BSP_BotStateDiveBombDone_Enter and 009D2530 BSP_BotStateTorpedoDone_Enter, so the indices are assigned when the follow state is entered, not at spawn. docs/PLANE_FORMATION.md. | CORRECTION (same packet): bsp.py ghidra callers returned four call sites; tools/callsite_census.py returns NINE - 007ED645, 007EE06A, 007F3A11, 007F4BFA, 009A48B8, 009AD1AF, 009B662F, 009BEDE4, 009D2558. 007F4BFA is inside 007F4580 BSP_PlaneSquadron_AttachLuaSelfAndSpawnPlanes, with 007F4BEE MOV ECX,ESI (the squadron) immediately before it, just past the 007F4B43..007F4B6E attach. So the formation indices are assigned AT SPAWN as well as on promote, leave and follow-state entry; the earlier sentence in this record saying they are assigned only when the follow state is entered is withdrawn.
